--- title: "Post-Transplant Cyclophosphamide Meta-Analysis" subtitle: "Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of PTCy vs alternative GVHD prophylaxis platforms" date: 2026-05-28 --- ## Abstract ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Background.** Post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) has become widely adopted for GVHD prophylaxis in allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation, yet comprehensive quantitative evidence synthesis across survival, GVHD, and infection outcomes — and across comparator regimens — has been lacking. **Methods.** We conducted a Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of observational studies comparing PTCy to (1) CNI+MTX/MMF-based regimens (Comparison 1; k = 6–35 across outcomes) and (2) ATG-based regimens (Comparison 2; k = 5–12). Primary outcomes included overall survival (OS), non-relapse mortality (NRM), acute GVHD grade II–IV, CMV reactivation, bloodstream infection (BSI), and invasive fungal infection (IFI). Steroid-mediation models (M2) tested whether GVHD-driven steroid exposure confounded observed effects. **Results.** PTCy was associated with improved OS (C1: OR 0.77 [0.71–0.83]; C2: OR 0.69 [0.61–0.78]) and reduced aGVHD (C1: OR 0.63; C2: OR 0.59) across both comparators. NRM benefit was substantially or completely mediated by steroid exposure in both comparisons. CMV reactivation showed a direction reversal: increased with PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.41 [1.20–1.65]) but decreased vs ATG (OR 0.77 [0.60–0.99]), consistent with a T-cell depletion depth hierarchy. BSI risk was elevated in both comparisons (C1: OR 2.39; C2: MH OR 2.03). **Conclusions.** PTCy provides consistent survival and GVHD advantages regardless of comparator. The CMV direction reversal establishes that infection risk is determined by the relative depth of T-cell depletion, not by any intrinsic PTCy property. NRM benefit is steroid-mediated. GRADE certainty is LOW for OS and aGVHD, VERY LOW for other outcomes. ::: --- ## Executive Summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pd <- do.call(rbind, list( or_summary(post_os, "b_ptcy_binary", "OS", Filled circles represent direct-effect models (M1); open circles represent steroid-adjusted models (M2). The dashed vertical line marks OR = 1 (no effect). OR < 1 favours PTCy for all outcomes.](index_files/figure-html/fig-exec-summary-1.svg){#fig-exec-summary} ::: ::: ### Key Findings ::: {.key-finding} **1. Survival and GVHD benefit.** PTCy was associated with reduced overall mortality and acute GVHD in both Comparison 1 (vs CNI+MTX/MMF) and Comparison 2 (vs ATG). The effect was consistent in magnitude and direction across comparators. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **2. NRM is steroid-mediated.** The apparent NRM benefit was substantially or completely attenuated after adjusting for GVHD-driven steroid exposure in both comparisons, indicating that PTCy reduces NRM indirectly — through fewer GVHD episodes and less corticosteroid toxicity. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **3. CMV direction reversal.** PTCy increased CMV reactivation vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.41) but *decreased* it vs ATG (OR 0.77). This reversal confirms that CMV risk is ordered by the depth of T-cell depletion (CNI < PTCy < ATG), not by any intrinsic PTCy property. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **4. BSI elevated in both comparisons.** Bloodstream infection risk was approximately doubled with PTCy regardless of comparator (C1: OR 2.39; C2: MH OR 2.03), though the C2 estimate is based on only 3 studies with heterogeneous definitions. ::: ### Summary of Evidence ::: {#tbl-exec-summary .cell tbl-cap='Summary of primary outcomes across both comparisons.'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Outcome, ~Comparison, ~k, ~N, ~`OR [95% CrI]`, ~`P(directional)`, ~Certainty, "OS", "C1", 35, 17661, "0.77 [0.71\u20130.83]", "P(<1) = 100%", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "OS", "C2", 10, 10624, "0.69 [0.61\u20130.78]", "P(<1) = 100%", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "NRM", "C1", 15, 2081, "0.86 [0.70\u20131.08]", "P(<1) = 90%", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "NRM", "C2", 5, 1186, "0.65 [0.43\u20130.97]", "P(<1) = 98%", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "C1", 24, 3837, "0.63 [0.54\u20130.74]", "P(<1) = 100%", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "C2", 6, 784, "0.59 [0.42\u20130.84]", "P(<1) = 100%", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "CMV", "C1", 18, 3357, "1.41 [1.20\u20131.65]", "P(>1) = 100%", "\u2295\u2295\u2296\u2296 LOW", "CMV", "C2", 12, 1267, "0.77 [0.60\u20130.99]", "P(<1) = 98%", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "BSI", "C1", 6, 1319, "2.39 [1.85\u20133.10]", "P(>1) = 100%", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "BSI", "C2", 3, 613, "2.03 [1.33\u20133.09]\u2020", "p = 0.001", "(\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296)", "IFI", "C1", 8, 3816, "0.73 [0.53\u20131.00]", "P(<1) = 97.5%", "\u2295\u2296\u2296\u2296 V.LOW", "IFI", "C2", NA, NA, "\u2014", "\u2014", "\u2014" ) |> kable(align = c("l", "c", "r", "r", "c", "c", "c")) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = TRUE) |> footnote(symbol = c("Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect estimate; formal GRADE not performed at k\u00a0=\u00a03.")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

The NRM benefit is fully steroid-mediated; the OS benefit is only partially mediated, suggesting an additional direct contribution. 2. **T-cell lymphodepletion pathway** (unintended): PTCy depletes CMV-specific and bacterial-specific T cells during engraftment. The CMV direction reversal across comparisons confirms this is a depth-of-depletion effect rather than a PTCy-specific one. ::: {.cell} ::: ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 8 %%| label: fig-mechanism %%| fig-cap: "Dual-pathway mechanistic framework for PTCy effects." flowchart LR PTCy --> A["↓ Alloreactive\nT cells"] PTCy --> B["↓ Pathogen-specific\nT cells"] A --> C["↓ aGVHD\nOR 0.59–0.63"] C --> D["↓ Steroid\nexposure"] D --> E["↓ NRM\n(fully mediated)"] D --> F["↓ OS\n(partially mediated)"] B --> G["↑ CMV vs CNI\nOR 1.41"] B --> H["↓ CMV vs ATG\nOR 0.77"] B --> I["↑ BSI\nOR 2.0–2.4"] style A fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style B fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style C fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style G fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style H fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style I fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a ``` --- *Navigate to individual pages using the menu above for detailed results, model diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, GRADE assessments, and risk-of-bias evaluation.*
